title: Average Vet Salary Australia: Award Rates, Hourly Conversion, and Take-Home Pay for 2026
description: Find the average vet salary Australia using Fair Work award rates. Convert hourly to annual for 38-hour weeks, see fortnightly pay, tax, and super. Updated for 2026.
salarySummary: Based on the Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award, a Level 1A veterinary surgeon earns a minimum of $34.20 per hour, equating to $67,582 per year for a 38-hour week over 52 weeks.

faqs.q: What is the average vet salary in Australia for 2026?
faqs.a: The minimum salary for a veterinary surgeon under the Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award ranges from $67,582 (Level 1A) to $95,593 (Level 4) per year for full-time work at 38 hours per week. Actual average earnings may be higher depending on experience, location, and private practice rates. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly earnings of $2,083.70, which would equate to about $108,352 annually, but this is not specific to vets.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a vet role?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, a Level 2 veterinary surgeon at $38.98 per hour earns $38.98 × 38 × 52 = $77,032 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: Does the casual loading apply to vet salaries, and how is it calculated?
faqs.a: Yes, casual veterinary surgeons receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate in lieu of leave entitlements. For a Level 1A vet, the casual rate is $34.20 × 1.25 = $42.75 per hour. This loading is paid on top of the base rate and is included in the annual estimate if you select the casual option. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Average Vet Salary Australia

When searching for the **average vet salary Australia**, the most reliable starting point is the Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award 2020, which sets minimum pay rates for veterinary surgeons, nurses, and other staff. As of 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission updated these rates, and they are enforced by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This article explains how to convert those hourly rates into annual, fortnightly, and take-home figures, including tax and superannuation.

### Award Minimum Rates for Veterinary Surgeons

The award classifies veterinary surgeons from Level 1A to Level 4. The minimum hourly rates and corresponding annual salaries (based on 38 ordinary hours per week, 52 weeks per year) are:

- Level 1A: $34.20 per hour → $67,582 per year
- Level 1B: $36.08 per hour → $71,300 per year
- Level 2: $38.98 per hour → $77,032 per year
- Level 3: $42.83 per hour → $84,628 per year
- Level 4: $48.38 per hour → $95,593 per year

These figures come directly from the award. They are the legal minimum; many vets earn above these rates, especially in private practice or with experience.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time vet working 38 hours each week, the annual gross salary equals the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, a Level 2 vet at $38.98 per hour earns $38.98 × 1,976 = $77,032.48 (rounded to $77,032 in the award).

If you are offered a salary instead, you can reverse the calculation: divide the annual salary by 1,976 to find the equivalent hourly rate. For instance, $84,628 ÷ 1,976 ≈ $42.83 per hour, matching Level 3.

### Fortnightly Pay

A fortnight is two weeks of work. For a 38-hour week, that’s 76 hours per fortnight. Multiply the hourly rate by 76 to get gross fortnightly pay. Using Level 1A: $34.20 × 76 = $2,599.20 per fortnight. This is useful for budgeting and comparing to typical pay cycles.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate instead of paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). For a casual Level 1A vet, the rate becomes $34.20 × 1.25 = $42.75 per hour. The annual estimate for a casual working 38 hours every week would be $42.75 × 1,976 = $84,474. However, casuals may not work consistent hours, so actual earnings vary. Use [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) to see how this affects your pay.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates for vets are significantly higher, starting at $34.20. This reflects the skill and responsibility required. The award also sets penalty rates for weekends and public holidays, which can boost earnings. See [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) for comparisons.

### Tax and Superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low incomes). For a Level 1A vet earning $67,582, the estimated tax (including Medicare) is approximately $11,267, leaving a take-home of about $56,315 per year. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed calculator.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For $67,582, that’s an extra $8,110 per year contributed to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay; it’s an employer obligation. Learn more at [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Comparing with ABS Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reported in May 2026 that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70. That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. While this is higher than the award minimum for vets, it reflects all occupations. The award rates are the floor; many vets earn above award, especially in specialist roles or metropolitan areas.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To personalise these calculations, visit [the timesheet](/). Enter your hourly rate (do not include casual loading—use the checkbox to add it), select your hours per week, and see annual, fortnightly, and monthly estimates with tax and super. The tool assumes 52 weeks and no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### Summary

The **average vet salary Australia** under the award ranges from $67,582 to $95,593 per year for full-time work. Converting hourly to annual is straightforward: hourly × 38 × 52. Remember that super is paid on top, tax is progressive, and casual loading adds 25%. For more award-specific pay rates, see [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).
